claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're enquiring about, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm enquiring about one child - my son Alex, who is 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 16, I need to ask: is Alex currently in approved education or training? This would include things like:
- Full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar qualifications)
- Approved training programmes (not paid for by an employer)

Could you let me know Alex's current education or training status?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. He left school and isn't studying anything right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know.

I have one more important question: has Alex recently left education or training, or registered with a careers service or the armed forces? If someone under 20 has recently left education/training and registers with certain services, there may be an extension period for Child Benefit eligibility.

Also, could you confirm whether Alex lives with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex does live with me, yes. But no, he hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces - he just left school and that's it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask a couple more questions to complete my assessment.

Are you currently living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Based on the information you've provided, I now have enough details to make an assessment of your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- **Age requirement**: Child Benefit is normally available for children under 16. For children aged 16-19, eligibility can continue only if they remain in **approved education or training**.

- **Alex's situation**: Since Alex is 16 and has left school without continuing in approved education or training, the basic eligibility criteria are not met.

- **Extension option not applicable**: There is a provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education/training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces. However, since Alex hasn't registered with either of these, this extension doesn't apply.

**What could change this?**

If Alex were to:
1. Start approved education or training (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or an approved training programme), or
2. Register with a careers service or the armed forces (which could extend eligibility for up to 20 weeks)

...then you may become eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.

If you have any questions or Alex's circumstances change, you can contact the Child Benefit Office for further guidance.
